title: SWMA: Symmetric Weighted Moving Average
summary: A moving average of the close with triangular weights, so the bars in the middle of the window count most and the ends count least.
description:
The Symmetric Weighted Moving Average averages the close over the last `period` bars with weights shaped like a triangle. With `half = (period - 1) / 2`, the bar `k` bars back weighs `half + 1 - |k - half|`: the middle bar weighs most, and the weights fall off evenly toward the newest and the oldest bar. The weighted sum is divided by the total of the weights.

A triangle of weights is what you get by smoothing with a simple average twice, so it removes more short-term noise than a single simple average of the same length. The line starts once `period` bars exist and always uses the close.
howToRead:
Read it as a smooth trend line. It is calmer than a simple average of the same length, so a turn in the line is less likely to be a single noisy bar. Price holding above a rising line describes an uptrend, and below a falling line a downtrend.

The weights peak in the middle of the window, so the line describes prices centred about `half` bars ago and lags by that much. Shorter periods follow price closely; longer ones show only the broad swing.

settings.label: Period
settings.description: How many bars the triangle spans. A longer period smooths more and lags more.

faq.q: Why are the middle bars weighted most?
faq.a: The triangle puts its peak at the centre of the window. That shape filters short noise better than equal weights, at the cost of a lag of about half the window.

faq.q: Can I choose a different price than the close?
faq.a: No. The calculation is fixed to the close, so there is no source setting.
Once `period` bars exist. Before that the oldest tap has no bar to read, so nothing is drawn.
